[]` (first element only), while the new EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents iterates all destinations and calls createEvent per credential, and Google's implementation was updated to match `credentialId` (`cal.credentialId === credentialId`) but O365 was not. For collective bookings handleNewBooking pushes team members' destinationCalendars into evt.destinationCalendar, so an Office365 host may receive the organizer's (e.g., Google) externalId in `/me/calendars/<id>/events`, and CalendarManager's catch swallows the failure, silently skipping the member's calendar. The mechanism is fully grounded in the diff.

judged_text: Office365 createEvent still resolves its target calendar from `destinationCalendar[0]` (the main host's calendar) instead of the destination entry matching the credential creating the event, so for collective bookings it builds `/me/calendars/<main-host-externalId>/events` with a calendar id foreign to the authenticating account. In a collective booking where hosts use different calendar accounts or providers (e.g., organizer on Google, member on Office365), the member's event creation calls the O365 API with the organizer's calendar id, fails, and is swallowed by CalendarManager's catch — the member's calendar silently gets no event.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and, for COLLECTIVE team events, appends other hosts’ destination calendars (`handleNewBooking.ts`: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`). However, `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` still destructures only the first entry (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];`) and builds the URL from that (`/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId}/events`). In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, events are created per-destination/credential, but the same `event` object (with multiple destination calendars) is passed, so the O365 implementation will always target the first calendar (likely the organizer’s), which can be foreign to the authenticating O365 credential for another host in collective bookings.
